method: Every expectation below was written from the text of the 2026 Montana Upland Game Bird Hunting Regulations (pp. 2, 4, 9, 10) and from Montana Fish, Wildlife & Parks' own upland game bird district, hunting district and restricted-area layers and the U.S. Census Bureau's TIGERweb reservation layer, each queried at the point on 2026-09-22 (scratchpad proofs/mt-verify-points.mjs), before any case was run against North Ground. A case that disagrees is a finding, never an expectation to edit.

cases.law: p. 9: mountain grouse (blue, ruffed, Franklin's) Sep. 01 – Jan. 01 statewide for residents and nonresidents alike; 3 in aggregate daily, possession four times the daily bag. FWP places Lewistown east of the Divide. No fact about the hunter changes it, so nothing is asked.
p. 9: the mountain grouse season opens Sep. 01.
p. 9: sharp-tailed grouse "Closed West of the Continental Divide." FWP places Missoula west of the Divide. No question can change it.
Butte sits near the Divide; FWP's own upland district layer places this point west of it, so sharp-tailed grouse is closed (p. 9).
p. 9: sharp-tailed grouse Sep. 01 – Jan. 01, but nonresidents on public or access-program land begin Sep. 11. On Sep. 05 the answer depends on residency.
p. 9: nonresidents on public lands and access-program lands begin Sep. 11.
p. 9: the nonresident public/access-program opening is Sep. 11.
p. 10: nonresident 3-day license holders on private land may hunt pheasants from Oct. 17; residents and season-license nonresidents on private land from Oct. 10.
p. 10: Oct. 17 for nonresident 3-day license holders on private land.
p. 10: youth-only pheasant season Sep. 19 – 20 for youth ages 15 and under; nobody else may hunt pheasant that weekend.

mentions: with the use of state licenses

cases.law: p. 4: the Commission has closed all lands within the exterior boundaries of Montana's Indian Reservations to upland game bird hunting with state licenses unless a cooperative agreement provides otherwise; the booklet names agreements only for the Flathead and (fee land) Crow reservations. TIGERweb places this point in the Northern Cheyenne Indian Reservation.

p. 4: on the Flathead Reservation a State–CSKT cooperative management agreement governs, with its own upland regulations North Ground has not certified. The state answer cannot be given, and neither can closure.

cases.place: Gates of the Mountains Game Preserve
cases.law: p. 10: Gates of the Mountains Game Preserve — closed to all hunting. FWP's restricted-area layer places this point inside it.
p. 9: partridge Sep. 01 – Jan. 01, except the described portion of Carbon County, open to Jan. 10. FWP's upland portion layer places this point inside it.
p. 9: outside the Carbon County portion the partridge season closes Jan. 01.

North Ground certifies no Montana deer rules (white-tailed deer is certified only in Canadian jurisdictions). The honest answer is UNKNOWN, never CLOSED, and the zone is FWP's own hunting district 309.

revision.evidence: The first run returned HTTP 400: /api/hunt/evaluate accepts only species North Ground certifies in some jurisdiction (isCertifiedSpecies), and elk is certified nowhere, so no one can ask it. The question the case exists for — a certified species with no Montana rules — is asked with white-tailed deer instead. The expected status is unchanged.

cases.law: FWP lists this point in the Gallatin Valley Weapons Restriction Area, a published restricted area whose upland rule, if any, is not in the regulations North Ground certified. §41A: a season is never claimed inside a published restricted area.
p. 2: the 2026 regulations are valid March 1, 2026 through Feb. 28, 2027. A date in the next licence year is not answered with them.
